text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The chairman of NATO's military committee, general Klaus Naumann, said in Vilnius on Tuesday that NATO's door remains open to all countries which aspire to membership.

- The new head of Vilnius police, Cheslovas Blazhys, was appointed on Tuesday. He replaces Vytautas Leipus, who resigned after French diplomat Patrick Donabedian was badly beaten and robbed in the capital on Sunday.
- Lithuanian border police detained 115 illegal immigrants in the last few days. The Pabrade foreigners' registeration centre now hosts 850 migrants.
- Lithuania's foreign trade deficit in the first half of 1997 rose to 2.798 billion litas from 1.756 billion litas in the same period in 1996.
- Lithuania and Germany signed an agreement on Tuesday to avoid double taxation on income and property.

- The presidents of Estonia, Latvia, Finland, Poland Belarus and Lithuania have confirmed they will participate in a regional conference in Vilnius on September 5. Russian Prime Minister Victor Chernomyrdin will represent President Boris Yeltsin at the conference.

- The patriarch of the Russian Orthodox Church, Aleksij II, who arrives in Vilnius on Friday, praised the relations between the Catholic and Orthodox faiths in Lithuania in an interview with the newspaper.
- Police arrested three youths suspected of robbing and savagely beating a French diplomat on Sunday. They said they spent the money, around $125, on gambling and alcohol.
- Denmark's Odense, which acquired an 84 percent stake in Baltijos Shipyard, intends to invest around 45 million litas in the company in 1997-1998.

- Baltic Beverages Holding managed to convince the small shareholders of Utenos Beverages to establish a joint-venture with their company. The shareholders rejected a competing offer from Denmark's Carlsberg on Monday.
- The head of the statistics department said on Tuesday that the country's gross domestic product was 8.15 billion litas in the first quarter of 1997, a 2.4 percent rise over the same period in 1996.

- The head of Klaipeda port, Valentinas Greichiunas, expects that 50 percent of the funds raised by the privatisation of the port's firms will be allocated to the reconstruction and upgrading of its facilities.
